import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 562

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/562](https://www.erdosproblems.com/562)
-/

open Combinatorics Filter Real
open scoped Asymptotics

namespace Erdos562

/--
Let $R_r(n)$ denote the $r$-uniform hypergraph Ramsey number: the minimal $m$ such that if we
$2$-colour all edges of the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph on $m$ vertices then there must be some
monochromatic copy of the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices.

Prove that, for $r \ge 3$,
$$ \log_{r-1} R_r(n) \asymp_r n, $$
where $\log_{r-1}$ denotes the $(r-1)$-fold iterated logarithm.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_562 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ r ≥ 3, (fun n ↦ log^[r - 1] (hypergraphRamsey r n)) =Θ[atTop] (fun n ↦ (n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos562

reformulations.difference: The shared hypergraphRamsey definition quantifies over colourings of all finite subsets of Fin m, whereas the source colours only the r-element subsets.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Restrict a colouring to the r-element subsets in one direction; extend an r-subset colouring by assigning false to all other subsets in the other direction. The monochromatic-set condition inspects only subsets of cardinality r, so the Ramsey property and its minimum are unchanged. Both the predicate equivalence and equality of the defining infima were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses norm-based IsTheta with total Real.log, instead of explicit positive two-sided inequalities for sufficiently large n.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each fixed r, finite Ramsey existence gives R_r(n) ≥ n, so every fixed iterated logarithm tends to infinity. Small-input logarithm conventions and absolute values therefore do not affect the asymptotic claim. The exact RHS is equivalent to: for every r ≥ 3 there exist positive c, C and a cutoff N such that c*n ≤ log^[r-1](R_r(n)) ≤ C*n for every n ≥ N. The constants and cutoff may depend on r, as required by the source's asymp_r notation. This unconditional equivalence was proved as problem_rhs_iff_explicit_bounds in the scratch file.
